issues.quote: I can tell you the regulator on the wall had stopped. Stopped with its master, I thought.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no information about the wall regulator, its stopping, or any reading connected to it.
issues.misreading: A solver could read the stopped regulator as a time-of-death clue, taking it to fix the moment of the murder or to show that a clock in the house was not running at the time, which the sheet does not support.

issues.quote: The old Morbier. It strikes its own hours from its own face and does not wait for anyone's permission.
issues.fact: D3 states only that the hall clock struck eleven a moment after the witness sat down again. The sheet does not say whether the hall clock agrees with the Temple bell or with the watches.
issues.misreading: The remark that the clock keeps its own time could lead a solver to suspect the hall clock runs differently from the bell and the watches, so that its eleven might not be the same moment as the bell's or the watch's readings.
